title: Hubble Interacting Galaxy NGC 3690
caption: Interacting galaxies NGC 3690 (Arp 299), imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3690, IC 694, Mrk 171, Arp 299, VV 118, KPG 288 · constellation Ursa Major · about 150 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration, and A. Evans (University of Virginia, Charlottesville/NRAO/Stony Brook University)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Hubble shows NGC 3690, also known as Arp 299, a pair of galaxies that swung close to each other some 700 million years ago. The encounter set off a fierce burst of star formation. It lies approximately 150 million light-years away in Ursa Major, the Great Bear.

Arp 299 has earned a reputation as a supernova factory. According to NASA's 2008 description, six supernovae had gone off in its outer reaches in the previous fifteen years or so. Massive stars live short lives, so a galaxy forming many of them can be expected to produce exploding stars at a high rate.

The system is counted among the ultra-luminous infrared galaxies and is thick with light-absorbing dust. Even so, enough violet and near-ultraviolet light escapes for it to appear as number 171 in B. E. Markarian's catalog of galaxies with excess ultraviolet emission. It is also the 299th object in Arp's Atlas of Peculiar Galaxies.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took this image. NASA has not published which filters were used or how colors were assigned.
understand.eye: As an ultra-luminous infrared galaxy, Arp 299 shines strongly in infrared light, which the eye cannot see.

explore: The image is one of 59 colliding-galaxy pictures released on 24 April 2008, the telescope's 18th anniversary. NASA notes that the majority of those observations were led by Aaron S. Evans of Caltech.
